system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against the Buyer Playbook

**Status note:** The Seller's cover note calls these "key negotiated positions" and "fair and balanced." Under playbook §0.4/§6.3 I treat them as the Seller's opening positions, not agreed or final terms. Nothing here is cleared unless it goes through our authority process. The Seller's facts are also as at 22 September 2026, and today is 6 November 2026, so each disclosed item needs a current status check.

## 1. Headline departures

| Area | Seller draft | Playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m (fallback 20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft; none given) | AUD 1.2m lower |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher; small claims excluded |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only recovery | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | First AUD 250k unrecoverable |
| General claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Frost approval) | 6 months shorter |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Fundamental regime removed |
| Limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum enforceable extent | No fraud carve-out |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public searches | Specific fair disclosure only | Deemed disclosure of everything |
| Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Excludes matters Buyer "had knowledge" of, including discoverable from data room/public records | Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Blanket exclusion |
| Bluefen (cl 3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion | Consent-on-delivery; endeavours insufficient |
| Riverlark (cl 2/7) | ~AUD 3.2m repaid by release "following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | Release after money moves |
| Employee bonuses (DL 5) | AUD 420k "a matter for the Seller," not in funds flow | Specific line item or seller-funded; must not silently drop out | Silent exclusion; on-costs unaddressed |
| Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden; preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180k unverified either way | Narrow indemnity |
| Export/privacy (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way | Materiality asserted without basis |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction | Characterisation asserted, not evidenced |
| Tax/IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain open; no unlimited liability; no resolution | Premature closure |
| Title (DL 10) | Evidenced by DD-012 share register | Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a seller-supplied internal source | Not independent proof |

## 2. Issue-by-issue reasoning and pushback

### A. Liability architecture (most material)

**General cap, thresholds and time limit.** Each Seller number lands at the weak end of the playbook. The 20%/AUD 4.8m cap matches our conditional fallback, but that match does not clear it. The fallback needs Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. Pushback: counter at 25% / AUD 6m, de minimis AUD 5,000, basket AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery once exceeded, and 24 months. Do not offer the fallbacks without Frost's written approval.

The excess-only basket is the most damaging mechanic. Under the Seller draft, the first AUD 250,000 of valid claims is unrecoverable, and claims under AUD 25,000 are ignored entirely. Reject it.

**"Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).** This is a hidden general-regime override. It would pull Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims into the general limits by default. Reject it. Keep each category's regime separate, with no default that flows from the general regime.

**Fundamental/Title on general terms.** Reject outright. Title and capacity claims need a 100% cap, at least six years, and must sit outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. "Administrative simplicity" is not a basis for this.

**Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).** These must not apply to fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct, to the maximum extent enforceable. Under the playbook no one may waive this carve-out. The Seller's "all Claims of any nature" wording must be narrowed. The non-reliance clause also needs the same fraud carve-out, or the Buyer could be left without a remedy for fraud.

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**General disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2).** Disclosing "every fact... in the data room" and the Accounts, statutory registers and public searches is deemed disclosure of everything, and it defeats specific warranty protection. Reject, and require specific fair disclosure that identifies the matter against the specific warranty.

**Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** Excluding anything "discoverable from the data room or public records" is a blanket exclusion. Delete it. If the Seller needs a knowledge qualifier, it must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. The qualifier must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### C. Conditions and completion mechanics

**Bluefen (cl 3/6.3; DL 2).** This is the most serious operational gap. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m, per DD-002). The Seller offers reasonable endeavours and treats consent as satisfied on delivery. The DL confirms no final written consent or evidence of satisfied conditions (cl 11.3) is in the data room. Reject. We need effective written consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough for a material customer consent, and consent-on-delivery is not acceptable.

**Riverlark (cl 2/7; DL 3).** The ~AUD 3.2m facility is not repaid, and the Seller proposes a release after Completion. Under the debt-free/cash-free baseline, require:
- a current payout figure;
- direct repayment from Completion funds;
- effective security releases.

If any release must follow Completion, it needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. The Seller's funds flow reflects "agreed price mechanics" but does not evidently show the Riverlark payout, so ask for a revised funds flow.

**Employee bonuses (DL 5; funds flow).** The AUD 420k in conditional bonuses is excluded from the draft funds flow and the Seller calls it "a matter for the Seller." Under the playbook it must be either a specific line item in the funds flow or seller-funded, and must not silently drop out. The DL also says payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are not addressed. Those on-costs are triggered amounts and are not quantified in the materials, so do not estimate them as fact. Require a specific seller-funded treatment that includes on-costs, and a payroll reconciliation.

### D. Specific risks

**Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4).** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and called "adequate." It is not adequate. DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180k open, which is not bank verification of non-payment, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. Broaden the indemnity to cover IP title and transfer and third-party claims, and preserve the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment). Treat the AUD 180k as unverified in both directions. The Seller's "adequate" is an assertion, not evidence.

**Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6; DD-006).** The Seller calls this "not expected to be material." The disclosure says the material does not establish whether anyone accessed the file, the scope (~1,240 records), or whether notification is required. Neither side has established a breach. Do not assert one, and do not assert the Seller's materiality conclusion either. Require:
- preservation of logs;
- completion of the investigation;
- regular written updates;
- confirmation of whether any notification obligation arises.

Whether a specific indemnity is warranted is a deal-team decision. The playbook does not prescribe one, so I have not recommended one.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k; DL 8).** The Seller calls these "ordinary-course operating costs," but DL 8 says the disclosure does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and asks that they be read together for timing and scope. Assess them: obtain the contracts, check for splitting of one commitment into three, and confirm terms. Do not classify them automatically as debt or apply a price deduction. The Seller's label is not evidence.

**Tax and IP (cl "general regime").** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not settled. Keep them open, with no unlimited liability and no resolution, and treat them under separate regimes.

**Title (DL 10; DD-012).** The Seller says title is evidenced by the share register. The register is a Seller-supplied internal source, not independent proof. Require:
- an independent company register extract;
- a PPSR and encumbrance search;
- evidence of authority, including board and shareholder resolutions.

**Lease and Mossvale (DD-007, DD-009; DL 7, 9).** The playbook does not address these directly, but both raise open questions. The DL says the office lease requires notification, not landlord consent, and that the Mossvale restriction does not, on its face, require consent for a share sale. Those are the Seller's characterisations. Check the lease and the Mossvale agreement, and confirm whether any change-of-control or assignment language is triggered. Do not accept the "not required" statements until verified.

## 3. Recommendations summary

**Reject outright:**
1. Fundamental/Title on general terms (Title and capacity need 100%, 6 years, outside the basket/de minimis/knowledge bar).
2. The "all Claims" limitation override (keep categories separate).
3. The whole-data-room, Accounts, registers and public-search general disclosure.
4. The blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion in cl 8.3.
5. Bluefen consent-on-delivery and the reasonable-endeavours standard.
6. The Riverlark post-Completion release without an undertaking and Frost approval.
7. The silent exclusion of the AUD 420k bonuses.
8. "Settled" tax and IP positions.
9. The excess-only basket.

**Counter (playbook positions):**
- General cap 25% / AUD 6m.
- De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period 24 months.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
- Specific fair disclosure only.
- Bluefen: effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion.
- Riverlark: payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases.
- Bonuses: specific line item or seller-funded, including on-costs.
- Ironquay: broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure.
- Title: independent evidence of title, encumbrances and authority.

**Require information and verification:**
- Current status of all disclosed items, since the Seller's facts are as at 22 September 2026.
- DD-006: log preservation, investigation, regular updates.
- Sandbar contracts and renewal terms.
- Lease and Mossvale review.

**Do not do without Amelia Frost's written authority:**
- Offer the 20%/AUD 4.8m cap.
- Offer the 18-month period.
- Agree any post-Completion Riverlark release without an irrevocable undertaking.

**Open for deal-team decision:**
- Whether a specific indemnity for DD-006 or Sandbar is warranted. The playbook does not prescribe one.
- Tax and IP terms, which remain open.

This is a commercial and legal analysis to support your deal team. Confirm the final positions with qualified NSW counsel before they go to the Seller.
=== END ADVICE ===
